stem.text: A length of metal wire is attached to a fixed point and hangs vertically. Masses are then suspended from the wire. Assume that the cross-sectional area of the wire remains constant.

stem.alt: Diagram of a metal wire hanging from a fixed point with masses suspended from its lower end.

stem.text: A stress–strain graph for the wire is plotted, as shown.

stem.alt: Graph with vertical axis labelled stress and horizontal axis labelled strain, both starting at 0, with a straight line from the origin and the area under it shaded.

stem.text: What is represented by the shaded area under the graph?

B.text: $\dfrac{\text{strain energy in the wire}}{\text{cross-sectional area of the wire}}$

C.text: $\dfrac{\text{strain energy in the wire}}{\text{original length of the wire}}$

D.text: $\dfrac{\text{strain energy in the wire}}{\text{original volume of the wire}}$
